title: Make the firstmate explainer page followable by newcomers
summary: Add cited plain-language lead-ins under the States, Counters, Transitions and Why sections, and one-line summaries and explained deciders on transition cards, so a reader new to firstmate can follow the page and glossary. The retry avoids the earlier failure by not adding fields to model.json, whose strict schema rejects unknown fields like `summary`; new prose goes in intro.json or site.rs, and cargo test is run before finishing.

defaults_applied.how: New tests assert lead-ins and the worked example render and cite existing claims; cargo test, clippy and fmt must pass.
Every new sentence cites an existing claim id.
The earlier failure came from the model.json schema, so the plan keeps new prose out of strict-schema files.
Wording is plain and defines each term on first use.
One focused change to the page generator, intro data, and docs.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Audience: a newcomer who has never seen firstmate, reading https://doodla.github.io/athena/.

The failed attempt broke because crates/athena-cap-study deserializes model.json with deny_unknown_fields, so a `summary` field was rejected; this attempt must not add unknown fields to model.json or must change the schema and its tests together.
Preferred approach: put new plain-language text in intro.json (or generated in xtask/src/site.rs from existing model data), each sentence citing an existing claim.

The 'basic example walked through start to finish' from the proposed request is satisfied by a short worked example in the intro that follows one piece of work through states and transitions, citing claims.
The producer runs cargo test --locked, clippy and fmt --check before finishing.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test --locked` (whole workspace); all tests pass, including athena-cap-study's rules tests that load studies/firstmate-work-handling/model.json, and new xtask tests asserting the lead-ins and example render and that an uncited new element is rejected.
Run `cargo run -p xtask -- site`; the rendered page has a plain-language lead-in under each of States, Counters, Transitions and Why saying what it shows and how to read it.
A newcomer can read the rendered Transitions cards without knowing ids: each card opens with a one-line plain summary, and the deciders 'agent' and 'code' are explained.
Every firstmate-specific term is defined in the glossary or at first use, and the page includes a short worked example from start to finish; every new sentence cites an existing claim.
Run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`; both are clean.
CHANGELOG.md records the change and docs/design/explainer-site.md matches the new page structure.

out_of_scope: Changing the firstmate study's claims, pin, or findings
Changing the deployment workflow or hosting of the site
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass chance than reference because the prior attempt of this same task was rejected on a failed test.
